column42: Sentiment analysis (SA) is an active and dynamic aspect of text mining that focuses on the automated analysis of subjectivity, opinions, and sentiments in textual material. The study explores new SA domains such as resource development, emotion recognition, and transfer learning. The study combines rule-based classification, machine learning, and supervised learning in a novel hybrid technique. The usefulness of this hybrid method is demonstrated through experiments on multiple datasets, including MySpace comments, product reviews, and movie reviews, resulting in improved classification efficacy as judged by both macro and micro-averaged criteria. The study also supports an additional semi-automatic approach in which classifiers cooperate to enhance overall performance. In this article, we have applied SVM, Decision tree, and Linear SVM to the Amazon review dataset and got the output in the form of performance metrics such as CPU-time and maximum memory usage. and we found that Depending on the linearity of the data, a linear SVM or a Decision Tree is more appropriate; select a linear SVM for clearly defined separations and a Decision Tree for intricate, non-linear interactions, customizing the model to the features of the dataset and the goals of the research.

column42: With an emphasis on Field-Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM) images, our goal is to enhance, classify, and segment 3D images acquired using a Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM). Based on the kind and concentration of doping present in the samples, these images are divided into three groups: Nd (Neodymium) doped cobalt chromite, La (Lanthanum) doped cobalt chromite and cobalt chromite in pure form. Our dataset includes ninety-three photos taken at different magnifications, offering a wide variety for additional processing and analysis. The effectiveness and appeal of the images are improved by the use of augmentation techniques. We use a new technique and pre-existing classical Deep Learning (DL) models to classify SEM pictures into different classes. While the 3D Residual Networks (3D ResNet) model achieves 40% average testing accuracy, the 3D Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) model shows 50% accuracy. But the categorization procedure is complicated by the similarities and complexity seen in each class of images as well as the inclusion of different magnification levels. We provide a unique algorithm ‘CompEx’ (Integrated Image compression and Feature extraction), a approach based on modular arithmetic to to identify unique characteristics from the pictures and to overcome these difficulties. In addition, we evaluate Cobalt Chromite samples and assess factors like porosity, particle size, and distribution using a variety of computer vision and image processing techniques

column42: With cardiovascular illnesses still posing a serious threat to world health, there is a growing demand for sophisticated diagnostic instruments that can precisely forecast the heart problems' severity. The study's main emphasis is leveraging deep learning methods for cardiac severity prediction with photos from an electrocardiogram (ECG). An extensive collection of ECG pictures covering different cardiac circumstances and degrees of severity are used to build models and assessment. CNNs, or convolutional neural networks, VGG-16, VGG-19 deep learning models are utilized to automatically retrieve detailed information from ECG pictures. Comparisons with conventional severity prediction based on ECG Convolution models are used to demonstrate and describe how the suggested deep learning method is superior. The incorporation using such Deep learning technology into medical practice has the potential to transform cardiac treatment by enabling prompt inter-ventions and enhancing the results for patients

column42: The kidneys, often overlooked yet vital for bodily equilibrium, serve a multifaceted role beyond filtration, governing crucial regulatory functions necessary for sustaining life. They orchestrate waste elimination, electrolyte balance, blood pressure regulations, and influence red blood cell production and vitamin activation. The advent of AI and deep learning has revolutionized medical diagnostics, especially in comprehending intricate renal complexities, facilitating rapid analysis of extensive datasets and transforming healthcare. Despite their resilience, kidneys remain susceptible to severe diseases such as Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), kidney stones, cysts, tumors, and infections, each presenting unique challenges in diagnosis and treatment. Detecting and categorizing renal pathology is crucial for timely diagnosis and effective treatment. This research centers on robust renal pathology classification utilizing deep learning models Convolutional Neural Network(CNN), ResNet, VGG16, and EfficientNet. Trained on a dataset of 12,466 renal images featuring cyst, normal, stone, and tumor classes, ResNet stood out, achieving outstanding results with 99.99% train accuracy, 99.91% test accuracy, and perfect weighted average precision, recall, and F1-scores. This underscores ResNet's reliability in accurately identifying renal pathologies, offering significant diagnostic support in clinical contexts

column42: To increase the survival rates for lung cancer, early identification and diagnosis are essential. The detection becomes crucial for a number of reasons, including visual similarity, heterogeneity, and low contrast variation. The several varieties of lung cancer that can be categorised histologically are determined by the kind of cells a pathologist can detect under a microscope. 15% of lung cancer cases are caused by small cell lung cancer (SCLC), while 85% of cases are caused by non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The three main types of NSCLC are lung adenocarcinoma, big cell carcinoma, and squamous cell carcinoma (SQCC). Deep learning models provides high level services to the healthcare domain. The proposed research focuses on applying deep learning models to segment and classify images of lung cancer histopathology. Images are segmented using the U-Net model. In order to categorise the different forms of lung cancer histopathology images, classification models like ResNet-50, VGG-16, and EfficientNet-B5 and Ensemble models of these three models were utilised. For the purpose of evaluating all the classifiers, performance metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 Score were computed. The U-Net model achieves 81% accuracy. ResNet-50 achieved an accuracy of 91%, VGG-16 94%, EfficientNet-B5 97%, and Ensemble model 99%, respectively. Among all models, an ensemble model is the most accurate

column42: This study describes an approach for optimizing a pretrained language model for Kannada text production. We leverage the GPT-2 architecture, which was first trained on a large Kannada corpus, to build a strong language model capable of comprehending and producing coherent Kannada text. The model is further refined using a dataset including pairs of prompts and their accompanying completions, allowing it to provide contextually appropriate and linguistically precise replies. The process is divided into two stages: pre-training to establish a generic language understanding, and strategy fine-tuning to improve model output quality. Due to computing resource constraints, the model was trained across fewer epochs on limited datasets; nevertheless, the suggested technique provides a foundation that may be extended and refined to increase performance. The evaluation of the fine-tuned model shows considerable gains in generating meaningful and contextually suitable Kannada text, indicating its potential applicability in a variety of Kannada-specific Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks. Attention maps visualization is also examined to highlight which words or tokens in a phrase have the most influence on predicting the following word in transformer-based models

column42: SEM (Scanning Electron Microscopy) takes nanoscale pictures, whereas DL (Deep Learning) analyses data using neural networks. Image interpretation is streamlined by the collaboration of SEM and DL, which automates SEM image analysis and material characterisation. This integration improves productivity by quickly extracting relevant information from enormous datasets, highlighting subtle patterns that would otherwise be difficult to detect manually. Authors of this article consider 3 classes of SEM images of various magnifications and a total of 93 images is being produced for analysis and processing. Authors intend to enhance, categorize, and segment the pictures collected. SEM pictures are classified based on doping substance with the host material pure Cobalt Chromite, Neodymium doped Cobalt Chromite and Lanthanum doped Co-balt Chromite. Image quality and appearance are improved via augmentation techniques. The similarity and complexity of images in all three classes and the inclusion of images of different magnification posed a challenge in classification which hinder the accuracy rate of classification process. So authors use the statistical results of the tests to create semi-automatic method for classifying and labeling pictures generated by the SEM. Authors propose a low complexity algorithm, aimed to extract features and increase model performance. This approach offers efficiency gains by minimizing time and computational resources compared to pre-trained models, while maintaining consistent classification results. Achieved a training and testing accuracy of 100% and 78.26% respectively. SEM pictures are also classified using CNN and pre-trained models VGG16, Inception v3. To evaluate and compare performance, comparative studies are used to measure model correctness. SEM images are segmented into regions of interest using an integrated technique that combined the watershed and contours. A segmented picture is used to calculate the surface area of a Cobalt Chromite sample. The surface area of material is determined to be 41,02,628 nm 2 .
